title: Programmatic Navigation
description: Learn how to navigate programmatically and protect routes.

data.text: Sometimes you need to navigate after an event — form submission, a successful API call, or a permission check. React Router provides hooks and components for programmatic navigation.
`useNavigate` returns a function you can call to change the route. It is the programmatic equivalent of clicking a `<Link>`.

data.title: useNavigate

data.text: `navigate` accepts a second options object. Use `replace` to swap the current history entry or `state` to pass hidden data.

data.title: Navigate with Options

data.text: Use the `<Navigate>` component to redirect declaratively inside JSX. This is perfect for protected routes.

data.title: Navigate Component

data.text: Wrap authenticated pages in a component that checks auth and redirects if needed.

data.title: ProtectedRoute

data.text: `useLocation` returns the current location object, including pathname, search, hash, and state passed via navigation.

data.title: useLocation
replace vs push
data.text: Use replace when the user should not go back (login, checkout). Use push (default) for normal navigation.

data.title: Exercise: Build a Login Redirect
data.description: Create a login form that redirects to the dashboard after successful authentication.
steps: Create a LoginPage with email and password fields.
On success, use navigate('/dashboard') with replace.
Create a ProtectedDashboard that redirects back to /login if not authenticated.
data.expectedOutcome: A login flow that redirects authenticated users and protects the dashboard.

items.question: Can I navigate outside of components?
items.answer: Not with useNavigate, which requires a component context. For navigation outside React, use the history instance or navigate programmatically via a ref.

items.question: What is the difference between Navigate and navigate()?
items.answer: Navigate is a component used declaratively in JSX. navigate() is the function returned by useNavigate for use inside event handlers or effects.

items.question: How do I prevent navigation?
items.answer: Use the useBlocker hook (React Router v6.4+) or a custom beforeunload listener for browser-level blocking.

items.question: Can I pass objects through navigation state?
items.answer: Yes. Navigation state is not reflected in the URL, making it ideal for passing temporary data like order IDs or form results.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: useNavigate changes routes programmatically from event handlers.
Navigate component redirects declaratively in JSX.
Protected routes guard pages by checking auth before rendering.
useLocation gives access to the current path, query, and state.
data.takeaway: Programmatic navigation gives you full control over routing behavior. Next, you will learn different approaches to styling React components.
